item.title: Patriots’ Kevin Byard is prepared for Ben Johnson’s shenanigans on TNF
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Patriots’ Kevin Byard is prepared for Ben Johnson’s shenanigans on TNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots are quite shorthanded on offense following Sunday’s 26-19 victory versus the New York Jets, and they only have a couple days to prepare for a road matchup against the Chicago Bears . Besides the injuries they will have to overcome, the Pats must stay alert when facing an innovative play-caller like head coach Ben Johnson. Veteran safety Kevin Byard regularly battled that offense last season, so he is taking it upon himself to get his teammates in the right mindset . “I practiced against Ben Johnson ’s offense,” the three-time First-Team All-Pro and former Bears star told reporters, per NBC 10 WJAR’s Nicole Menner. “You talk about scheme, and I know Ben, it being Thursday night he’s going to have some stuff up his sleeve. It’s a prime-time game, he’s going to want to show off his expertise, I would say. So, I’m just telling the guys {to have} great discipline, read your keys, play with great eyes, and after that, just fly around, make plays.” Kevin Byard (who spent the last 2 years on the Bears): Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "I practiced against Ben Johnson's offense. You talk about scheme, and I know Ben, it being Thursday night he's going to have some stuff up his sleeve." pic.twitter.com/oEGZ25d471 — Nicole Menner (@NicoleMenner) October 20, 2026 The Patriots placed Romeo Doubs on injured reserve due to a shoulder issue. A.J. Brown is still shaking off the rust after a long IR stint himself and could experience some discomfort by playing twice in a five-day span. The offensive line is also painfully undermanned, with center Ben Brown and guard Alijah Vera-Tucker both considered doubtful and offensive tackle Morgan Moses questionable after wearing a walking boot on Sunday. New England may need to lean on its defense in Week 7. Kevin Byard spent two years in Chicago and was a massive part of the franchise’s resurgence last season. He has not enjoyed nearly the same success with the Patriots thus far. The 33-year-old is still searching for his first interception (had seven in 2025 campaign) and is coming off a rough performance in which he missed three tackles versus the Jets. Byard still boasts loads of experience, however. Even when he is not operating at full capacity in the secondary, No. 31 can still help the defense get organized and composed for the Bears’ tricky offense. He is not going to let Ben Johnson catch New England off guard. But will his counsel be enough? Related: Patriots CB takes first step in injury return ahead of TNF clash vs. Bears Related: A.J. Brown sends heartfelt message to Eagles’ Jalen Hurts after blood clot diagnosis

item.title: ‘Brock Purdy Hasn’t Even Had a Bad Game’ — Ex-NFL LB Salutes ‘Undefeated’ 49ers QB for Playing ‘Near-Perfect Football’ Amid MVP Chants
item.description: Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) looks on during the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. © Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY The San Francisco 49ers are one of three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL, but they’re the only one with six wins rather than five. Boasting a top-five offense and defense, many would argue that the 49ers are the best team in football, and Brock Purdy’s stellar play is a big reason why. Four and a half years ago, all 32 teams, including the 49ers, passed on Mr. Irrelevant several times in the NFL Draft. Now, he’s getting MVP chants and earning extra praise from a former NFL linebacker turned football analyst. Emmanuel Acho is a Big Brock Purdy Guy It’s fair to say that Purdy, who became the NFL’s all-time passer rating leader on Monday night, has been one of the league’s best quarterbacks of the season. His NFL-leading 90.8 PFN Impact Score among QBs would back up what the eye test has shown. Six games into the season, former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho went on the “ Speakeasy ” podcast to state his belief that Purdy is playing the best football of his career. “I don’t think there are enough words to adequately describe what Brock Purdy is doing,” Acho said. “Because I don’t think people truly understand. We talked all the time about what Patrick Mahomes did when he didn’t have any true No. 1 wide receivers. You realize Brock Purdy has lost (Ricky) Pearsall, lost (De’Zhaun) Stribling, lost Deebo (Samuel), for this half lost Mike Evans, and still leads the NFL in touchdown passes. Brock Purdy has yet to play a bad game.” Purdy is tied with Kirk Cousins and Trevor Lawrence for the NFL lead with 14 touchdown passes through Week 6. Email is the preferred method for reporting scores. ⚽ GIRLS SOCCER - Division I North Kingstown 5, Mt. Hope 1 Daniella Sisco scored twice on each side of halftime and June Merchant dished out three assists as the Skippers eased past the Huskies, 5-1, in Division I. Sisco hit the net in the 39th and 42nd minutes, as North Kingstown broke open what was a 1-0 lead. She finished a hat trick in the 53rd minute when Merchant crossed in off the left side and Finola Gately fired home the last in the 63rd minute to complete the victory. The Skippers (8-3-4) took the lead for good late in the first half when Merchant whipped in a corner kick off the left. Reagan Farrell celebrated her return from a minor injury by redirecting the ball across the line, and North Kingstown had a 1-0 edge. The Skippers doubled the lead just before halftime. Braelyn O'Connor played a pretty diagonal ball off the left to Sisco, who found space beyond the defense and slotted home a textbook finish to make it 2-0. North Kingstown added on out of the break when Sienna Barron cut one back to Sisco off the right side to open a 3-0 advantage. Mt. Hope (5-6-4) played without star Emma Goglia (undisclosed injury) and could only manage one answer. Sara Nencka fired home from distance in the 77th minute to break up the shutout, a right-footed strike just under the crossbar. item.title: Warriors' Steph Curry gets good injury update, Brandin Podziemski gets bad news for Lakers opener
item.description: Warriors' Steph Curry gets good injury update, Brandin Podziemski gets bad news for Lakers opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors knew heading into training camp that they would be without Jimmy Butler after he tore his ACL last season. The roster was also lacking depth, so the team knew injuries would need to be kept to a minimum this season. However, at the start of training camp, the Warriors received more bad news. Center Kristaps Porzingis experienced a sudden health issue that left head coach Steve Kerr concerned. Yeah, I mean, you know, we want him back. He's a really talented player, and so we thought he was in a pretty good place. So it's definitely concerning. And so, as I said, all we're going to do is support him, give him every bit of medical help he can get, and emotional support, and hope he is back soon." Kerr said. Over the weekend, more injury concerns emerged as Brandin Podziemski and Steph Curry both dealt with injuries. Podziemski was dealing with a back issue, while Curry suffered an ankle injury. “During a scrimmage, Curry tried to make a turn near midcourt and immediately appeared to feel something in his right leg. The mood inside the arena — joyous and filled with fans for most of the day — instantly turned to concern. He made his way slowly back to the Warriors’ sideline, held his arms down at his sides, spoke with a member of the training staff and tried to shake it off. After a few seconds, Curry shook his head and gingerly made his way to the locker room with team personnel,” The Athletic’s Nick Friedell wrote. With the season beginning Wednesday against the Los Angeles Lakers , Curry appears to be ready to play, while Podziemski has been ruled out. “Brandin Podziemski is out for the Warriors tomorrow night in Los Angeles. Lower back soreness. He played all 82 games last season but will miss the opener this season against the Lakers. Steph Curry is probable,” ESPN’s Anthony Slater wrote. The Warriors appear to have avoided a major injury concern with Curry, while the team will likely take precautions to ensure Podziemski’s back issue does not worsen. Golden State knows how important its depth will be throughout the season, making the health of its key players crucial. Curry’s condition will be worth monitoring Wednesday night to see how he responds to the ankle issue. The Warriors and Lakers are set for an intriguing matchup to open the season, and Golden State will hope to have its star guard ready to go. item.title: Spurs kickoff new NBA season with fresh batch of H-E-B commercials
item.description: Devin Vassell, De'Aaron Fox, Keldon Johnson and the Spurs coyote in H-E-B's new "Hardball" commercial. (Courtesy of H-E-B) The 2026-27 NBA season is officially underway, and that means the San Antonio Spurs have renewed their quest for a sixth championship. That also means San Antonio locals will see plenty of their Silver & Black superstars on their TV screens in humorous commercials with the city's favorite grocery chain. H-E-B and the San Antonio Spurs have once again partnered to film a series of fun commercials for the homegrown grocery giant. This season will see the likes of Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Keldon Johnson and Dylan Harper all appear on screen to promote the Spurs and H-E-B. item.title: UConn men's basketball team impressive in intense exhibition win over Michigan State
item.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Head coach Dan Hurley of the UConn Huskies reacts in the first half of the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Breslin Center on October 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) (Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) EAST LANSING, Mich. - It wasn't the Final Four, Elite Eight or Sweet 16, where these two powerhouse programs have faced each other over the past 18 years. It was merely Exhibition Two for both teams, though you'd have a hard time believing that based on the large, rowdy Breslin Center crowd and the intense, physical play on the floor. In a game that didn't count but certainly looked like it did, the UConn men's basketball team topped Michigan State 78-70 on Tuesday night. Nik Khamenis scored 19 points, including a spinning, teardrop jumper with 1:09 left to pretty much seal the deal, and Silas Demary Jr. added 16. Freshman Colben Landrew added 13 points and five rebounds. Na'jai Hines, back in the starting lineup after beginning last week's Syracuse exhibition on the bench, scored eight points before fouling out, and Nils Machowski chipped in seven points off the bench. Michigan State All-American candidate Jeremy Fears Jr. led all scorers with 23 points. It's not even Halloween yet, but the Huskies' offense appeared in March form, particularly in the second half. UConn darted passes around the perimeter for 3's and to cutters for layups and shot 57 percent (16-for-28) from the floor and 6-for12 from 3 over the final 20 minutes. The Huskies had 13 assists on 16 field goals in the latter half and 21 dimes on 27 makes for the game. Meanwhile, UConn held Sparty to 40 percent shooting overall and a mere 3-for-20(15 percent) from 3. One negative for the Huskies: they were 14-for-22 from the foul line, and for the second game in a row, their starting center fouled out. Otherwise, it was hard not to be impressed with UConn overall on Tuesday in a game that meant nothing but said an awful lot. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: Bucks’ Kyle Kuzma reveals Milwaukee’s plan to show support for Brewers in World Series
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Bucks’ Kyle Kuzma reveals Milwaukee’s plan to show support for Brewers in World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Milwaukee is about to host its first World Series game in more than four decades , and the Milwaukee Bucks do not plan on missing it. Kyle Kuzma told reporters that the entire Bucks team is going to try to make its way to Game 1 of the World Series to support the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday night at American Family Field. The veteran forward added that he has never attended a World Series game before. The timing works out for the Bucks, but only barely. Milwaukee hosts the Chicago Bulls in its home opener on Friday at Fiserv Forum, then visits the Philadelphia 76ers the following night. According to Kuzma, the team has enough time after the home opener to catch some of Game 1 before its flight out that night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bucks helped make that possible themselves. Once it became clear the Brewers would host Game 1 on the same night, the franchise moved its home opener from 7 p.m. to 3 p.m. local time to avoid a conflict . “The Bucks are proud to move our home opener to 3 p.m. in recognition of this historic occasion,” the team said in a statement. It is a big moment for the city. The Brewers last reached the World Series in 1982, when they lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games, and the franchise has never won a championship. Milwaukee punched its ticket this time by sweeping the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS. Standing in the way are the Tampa Bay Rays, who beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the ALCS on Monday to take the series 4-2. Like the Brewers, the Rays have never won a World Series, having fallen short in 2008 and 2020. That guarantees a first-time champion either way. Game 1 is set for 7 p.m. CT on Friday in Milwaukee , with Game 2 also at American Family Field on Saturday. Before any of that, Kuzma and the Bucks have their own business to handle . Milwaukee opens its regular season on Wednesday against the Washington Wizards in D.C. Then comes a busy stretch, with a home opener, a trip to the ballpark and a road game in Philadelphia all packed into about a day. item.title: 🎥 Keeper blunder fatal! Vasco fight, Boca oust them at Maracanã
item.description: 🎥 Keeper blunder fatal! Vasco fight, Boca oust them at Maracanã Vasco failed to end their nearly 26-year wait to reach an international tournament final. After winning 1-0 at La Bombonera, Vasco faced Boca Juniors at a Maracanã that welcomed them with a huge celebration on Tuesday night (20). But they were beaten 3-1 in front of 66,026 fans in the second leg of the Sudamericana semifinal. They had been competing on three fronts and now turn their attention to the battle against relegation in the Brasileirão and the Copa do Brasil semifinal. The Argentine side, meanwhile, await the winner of Montevideo City Torque and Atlético Mineiro as they chase their third Sudamericana title. They advanced with a 3-2 aggregate victory. Check back soon for the highlights. Boca are ruthless as Vasco struggle The Argentine side's "dream scenario" became reality before the fourth minute. Blanco delivered a corner and Di Lollo rose above Sosa to head home. The nerves were evident even before Boca's goal. And they only grew. Adson and Bruno Duarte went for the same ball, for example. Vasco managed to create chances before halftime. But they lacked accuracy. There was no shortage of that at the other end. Another individual mistake led to a Merentiel goal (34'), putting Boca ahead on aggregate. There were several poor individual performances in Pedro Emanuel's side. And a ruthless Boca showed no mercy. Vasco return a 'different' team Vasco came out for the second half with Marino and Brenner. And with a very different approach, trying to pin their opponents back. It was Boca's turn to struggle without the ball. Puma Rodríguez was Pedro Emanuel's third substitute. And he brought Vasco back into the tie by finishing off a lovely team move in the 66th minute. Léo Jardim lets it slip After suffering a grade 2 injury 11 days earlier and making a remarkable recovery, the midfielder who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina was brought on in the second half. He had been quiet. But he would prove decisive. He tried his luck, and the ball swerved, catching out Léo Jardim, who let it in (88'). A goal from Boca's only chance of the second half. 📸 Wagner Meier - 2026 Getty Images Vasco kept fighting. But they could not even force a penalty shootout. What next❓ Boca will face either Montevideo City Torque or Atlético Mineiro in the final. Atlético hold a commanding lead after winning 3-0 at Arena MRV. The return leg takes place on Wednesday (21), kicking off at 7 p.m. Brasília time. Vasco, meanwhile, will turn their attention back to the Brasileirão. On Saturday (24), they face Corinthians at São Januário. Winless in two matches, Vasco—who have a game in hand—currently sit 15th with 35 points. Their next opponents are winless in nine league games and sit 16th with 33 points. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: The New York Knicks legends who handed out NBA Championship rings, including Walt Frazier
item.description: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images The new legends of the New York Knicks received their NBA championship rings from all the past legends in franchise history. Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, and all the other New York Knicks stars brought a championship to the franchise after 53 years in 2026. It had been a long wait for the organisation, but that also made the win that much more special. Before they opened their 2026-27 NBA campaign against the Philadelphia 76ers, the Knicks celebrated their amazing accomplishment by raising the banner and giving the stars their well-earned rings. They got those from some of the biggest names in franchise history. Walt Frazier, Bill Bradley, and Willis Reed’s wife among those handing out the Knicks stars their rings The 1973 New York Knicks team battled past the Baltimore Bullets and the 68-win Boston Celtics to reach the NBA Finals. There, they beat the Los Angeles Lakers 4-1 to claim their second title. The same core had also won it all in 1970, making them all franchise legends. The starting five for that 1973 team were all the people who gave the new champs their rings at Madison Square Garden. Walt Frazier, Bill Bradley, Dave DeBusschere, and Earl Monroe were on hand for the beautiful moment. Willis Reed’s wife, Gale Reed, took his place. This was a very special moment in franchise history, and it is very fitting for there to have been a ‘changing of the guard’ for the Knicks. There are new franchise legends in town who can point to the banner they helped put up, although they will want more. The Knicks won two championships in four years in the 70s, and this team will start this season likely hoping to defend their title in 2026-27. If they do that, the likes of Brunson and Hart will have made themselves as big as all of the names who handed them their rings. item.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves hilariously reveals reaction to LeBron James in 76ers uniform
item.description: © Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Lakers’ Austin Reaves hilariously reveals reaction to LeBron James in 76ers uniform appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After spending eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers , LeBron James decided to leave in free agency. James would join a stacked Philadelphia 76ers team with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown, and the Lakers would then make a plethora of signings in their first opportunity to build a team properly around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. For Reaves, however, it remains a bit of whiplash for him to see James don a jersey other than the Lakers’. After all, he did spent five seasons in the same locker room with James, and seeing him in Philly colors requires some getting used to. Reaves, in fact, revealed his hilarious reaction to seeing James don a new uniform during preseason. “I almost texted [LeBron], told him he looked crazy,” Reaves told reporters ahead of the Lakers’ season-opener on Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors, via Carlos Yakimowich of The Sporting Tribune. “It’s different. But you know, that’s my guy. I wish him the best and I’ll definitely watch [the 76ers’ season opener vs. the New York Knicks].” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Austin Reaves on seeing LeBron in a diffrent uniform. “I almost texted him and told him he looked crazy.” (asked by @DStarkand ) pic.twitter.com/hg1PYjr1Tr — Carlos Yakimowich (@CarlosYakJr) October 20, 2026 James was incredible for the Lakers during the 2026 NBA playoffs, averaging 23.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 7.3 assists as he and Reaves put up a gallant stand amid Doncic’s injury woes. But in the end, the 41-year-old star wanted another legitimate chance to compete for a title, and he saw that joining the 76ers furthers that goal of his. The Lakers do have a talented roster, but the Western Conference is simply too much of a bloodbath. Reaves, at the very least, appears to be in line for his best season yet. Last year, he put up 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 5.5 assists per contest. Now, he is the legitimate second scoring option for the Lakers and he’ll be taking control of the offense alongside Doncic. It remains quite a marvel that Reaves, who went from a beloved bench guy in his rookie year, endearing himself to James in the process, has blossomed into this big of a star for the Lakers. item.title: "Fundamentals will triumph everything else": USC preps for Wisconsin
item.description: LOS ANGELES --- The USC Trojans head into Camp Randall Stadium this Saturday, having learned the same lesson in their past two contests: close games get decided by fundamentals and playmaking, not emotion. After escaping Washington at home and outlasting Penn State's White Out, the Trojans used their bye week to recover physically. They also made sure that lesson would stick before facing a Wisconsin defense built in a similar image. Head coach Lincoln Riley made clear that returning from the week of isn't only about riding the momentum from Happy Valley. "Our deal is very process and standard oriented," Riley said. "The reality is we've won every game but one this year, and in those games we found things we did well and things that we didn't do well...our process stays very consistent." That process showed up specifically on the offensive line in the form of true freshman Vlad Dyakonov, who was thrust into his first career start at Penn State on short notice. Fellow offensive lineman Justin Tauanuu said the moment didn't rattle him at all. "The most impressive part about him is just him being calm, not having much nervousness going in...especially going into a big atmosphere such as Penn State," Tauanuu said. "I'm really impressed with how he played." Tauanuu credited that composure to a next-man-up culture the room has leaned on to navigate injuries this season. He said the group's focus this week is strictly fundamental against a Wisconsin defensive front that he expects to serve as a strong test. "Really just focusing on our fundamentals...going against great players like that, you always have to go back to the fundamentals, and the fundamentals will triumph everything else." Badgers' outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks poses to be one of those players that will give the Trojans trouble, with his two and a half sacks and two forced fumbles leading the team. Wisconsin, despite suffering a loss, was just the second team this season to hold No. 9 UCLA to 17 points in a game. Quarterback Jayden Maiava identified Wisconsin's linebacker core as critical to their success. "They're kind of the heart of their defense," he said. "As you see it on film, [they] kind of get the guys rolling on D, and we're just excited to go out there against those guys." Maiava also took time to talk about one of his wide receivers, sophomore Tanook Hines. He pointed Hines out as someone whose growth and leadership have gone a long way for the receiver room as a whole. "Those guys are getting really close every single day," Maiava said. item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES --- The USC Trojans head into Camp Randall Stadium this Saturday, having learned the same lesson in their past two contests: close games get decided by fundamentals and playmaking, not emotion. After escaping Washington at home and outlasting Penn State's White Out, the Trojans used their bye week to recover physically. They also made sure that lesson would stick before facing a Wisconsin defense built in a similar image. Head coach Lincoln Riley made clear that returning from the week of isn't only about riding the momentum from Happy Valley. "Our deal is very process and standard oriented," Riley said. "The reality is we've won every game but one this year, and in those games we found things we did well and things that we didn't do well...our process stays very consistent." That process showed up specifically on the offensive line in the form of true freshman Vlad Dyakonov, who was thrust into his first career start at Penn State on short notice. Fellow offensive lineman Justin Tauanuu said the moment didn't rattle him at all. "The most impressive part about him is just him being calm, not having much nervousness going in...especially going into a big atmosphere such as Penn State," Tauanuu said. "I'm really impressed with how he played." Tauanuu credited that composure to a next-man-up culture the room has leaned on to navigate injuries this season. He said the group's focus this week is strictly fundamental against a Wisconsin defensive front that he expects to serve as a strong test. "Really just focusing on our fundamentals...going against great players like that, you always have to go back to the fundamentals, and the fundamentals will triumph everything else." Badgers' outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks poses to be one of those players that will give the Trojans trouble, with his two and a half sacks and two forced fumbles leading the team. Wisconsin, despite suffering a loss, was just the second team this season to hold No. 9 UCLA to 17 points in a game. Quarterback Jayden Maiava identified Wisconsin's linebacker core as critical to their success. "They're kind of the heart of their defense," he said. "As you see it on film, [they] kind of get the guys rolling on D, and we're just excited to go out there against those guys." Maiava also took time to talk about one of his wide receivers, sophomore Tanook Hines. He pointed Hines out as someone whose growth and leadership have gone a long way for the receiver room as a whole. "Those guys are getting really close every single day," Maiava said. They all bring different things,” UConn coach Danny Hurley said. “If they could figure out the center thing, they could be one of the best teams in the country. “They have everything you need to be a national championship contender. Carlos Medlock Jr. is figuring out this new level — mostly the length and strength he’s got to deal with. I think he’ll get there. The key for him will be to be solid as a backup point guard as the season gets going. MSU doesn’t need him to make shots. Great if he does. But they need him to run the show. He was 1-for-7, with one assist and one turnover in 10 minutes. He shouldn’t be taking seven shots in 10 minutes. Ethan Taylor is someone to watch. He showed some things — on the drive, on the glass. He finished with five points and two rebounds in 11 minutes at center. Talking to him last week, he is determined to be a factor this season. I wouldn’t rule that out, especially if the center position is this unsettled. Defensively, he lost his assignment a couple times. If he’s solid on that stuff and strong enough to hold his ground, he’ll be in the rotation. 3. Those 3-point shooting numbers, oh my MSU has been through this before, so it's easy to get nervous about a 3-for-20 shooting night from beyond the arc. This should be a decent shooting team, though. There are too many good-to-capable shooters on this roster. But you also have to make shots. You can't just be known as a guy who can. Kur Teng, who is coming back from a foot injury, missed all three 3s Tuesday. He’s at this level because he’s a shooter. He's got to make them. Jordan Scott missed both of his 3s. Jesse McCulloch only took one and missed it. He should take more. Carlos Medlock tried four — he should try less. Jasiah Jervis went 2-for-5. Jeremy Fears Jr. hit the only other one on a brutal night collectively from deep. The center position is part of what this team will have to figure out. So, too, is having enough shooters on the floor at one time. And, ultimately, the shooters are the guys who make shots and do so at a clip that’s respected by opponents enough to be on the scouting report. It’s one exhibition game, with a lot of bizarre lineups. It’s way, way too soon to react with concern. But MSU does need three or four guys it can count on to make shots from beyond the arc. Katya Henry is claiming that Tyler Herro sent “inappropriate” and “aggressive” texts to her amid their custody battle. item.title: BYU heads to Florida riding lofty hype, momentum, kudos
item.description: BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake talks to an official during the second half of a football game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at LaVell Edwards Stadium, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, in Provo. BYU won the game 28-24. | Erin Hooley, Deseret News BYU heads to UCF in Orlando, fighting to set aside emotions from the historic home win over Notre Dame. It will require focus, avoiding the “rat poison” of listening to praise, and laborious work at practice. After climbing to No. 2 in the AP Top 25 rankings, can the Cougars climb aboard the execution train and make all this magic work on the longest road trip of the year? If they’re for real, yes. Head coach Kalani Sitake is selling his mantra hard: Stay hungry and humble. He means it. This week is the culmination of what he’s been talking about all season. After BYU climbed in the rankings, QB Bear Bachmeier earned National Player of the Week from AP. Linebacker Cade Uluave, BYU’s leading tackler in the game, was named the Big 12 Defensive Player of the Week. Rat poison? That’s what former Alabama coach Nick Saban said can set back a winning football team when they read about themselves on social media and let it go to their heads. Here are some examples of statistical rat poison: BYU’s strength of record is now No. 1 in the country ahead of Kentucky, UCLA, Ohio State, Miami and Indiana, in that order. BYU is the only team in the nation to start the past three seasons with a perfect 6-0 record. BYU had 11 tackles that went backward against No. 2 Notre Dame. item.title: How to Watch Gonzaga Basketball in the 2026-27 Season
item.description: SPOKANE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 24: Davis Fogle #4 of the Gonzaga Bulldogs drives against Mookie Cook #1 of the San Francisco Dons during the second half of the game at McCarthey Athletic Center on January 24, 2026 in Spokane, Washington. (Photo by Robert Johnson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Gonzaga Bulldogs’ move to the Pac-12 Conference not only means new opponents, but also new television networks. On October 14th, the league’s broadcast schedule for the 2026-27 season was announced by the revamped league. Through their 31 regular-season contests, the Zags will reappear on ESPN, FOX, TNT, and CBS/CBS Sports Network. Broadcast schedule dropped 📺⏰ 📰Read More: https://t.co/bGWc9x3t0D 🗓️Full Schedule: https://t.co/3r3tuoSvDP pic.twitter.com/ouI1j6F7gp — Gonzaga Basketball (@ZagMBB) October 14, 2026 The season opener for coach Mark Few’s team comes against Purdue in Las Vegas on November 2nd, which can be viewed on TNT or truTV. Gonzaga’s one stretch of games on the ESPN Networks will also take place in Las Vegas, at the Players Era Festival. The first-round matchup versus Kansas State is on ESPN on November 24th. The Zags will play three games televised on CBS: Michigan State on December 19th, Oregon in the Battle in Seattle on January 30th, and San Diego State in the Kennel on February 27th. While fans are familiar with watching the Bulldogs play on those popular networks, the Pac-12 Conference signed a five-year media rights partnership with multiple new stations that earns the university a 100 percent full media share. The estimated earnings are reported somewhere between $7 million and $12 million annually despite not having a football program. The CW, which can be viewed on ESPN Unlimited, will air six Gonzaga games from their upcoming slate. Nine of the other games for the Zags will air on USA Network. Gonzaga only has two contests scheduled to air locally in Spokane on KHQ: the exhibition matchup with Lewis-Clark State on October 28th, and the home opener with New Mexico State on November 7th. That means only two games with the play-by-play voice of Greg Heister and the analysis from Richard Fox. With color commentator Dan Dickau signed on to the CBS Sports Network, there is a good chance that Zag fans will hear plenty of the legendary Bulldog’s takes, as Gonzaga has six games airing on there. The most unusual network airing a Zag contest is Amazon Prime Video, when Gonzaga plays Duke in Detroit on February 20th. Prime Video signed a three-game deal with the Blue Devils, making it the first time the streaming service will broadcast college basketball. The best subscription service for fans to watch all these battles from the 2026-27 season would be either YouTube TV or Hulu Live. Gonzaga’s upcoming exhibition at Arkansas on October 24th is a bit tougher to view, airing on SEC Network+.

item.title: Green Bay Packers: Matt LaFleur calls Josh Jacobs “an elite level back”
item.description: Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that Josh Jacobs ‘ workload against the Detroit Lions will be decided during the week, as the running back returns to practice for the first time this season. Dec 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) during the game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The NFL placed Jacobs on the commissioner’s exempt list Aug. 30. He pleaded no contest Sept. 10 in Brown County to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges stemming from a May incident. The league has since removed him from the list and made him eligible for Sunday’s game at Ford Field. Its review of his off-field situation under the personal conduct policy continues. Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reported Saturday that Jacobs “will immediately return as the Packers’ starting running back” at Detroit, as Wisconsin Sports Heroics reported . Matt LaFleur calls Josh Jacobs “an elite level back” LaFleur said after Sunday’s 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys that Jacobs could give the offense a spark. He repeated it Monday. “Well, I think he’s an elite level back. He’s certainly not going to hurt it,” LaFleur said. “So I think he can provide a spark. I think that’s what I said last night.” How many snaps Jacobs plays in Detroit has not been set. “I think that’s going to be determined throughout the course of the week, see where he’s at, see how he’s feeling, and then we’ll make a decision,” LaFleur said. The exempt list kept Jacobs away from the practice field but not the building. “So he could go to meetings. He could lift with our strength coaches and condition with them,” LaFleur said. “He couldn’t go to any of the team activities, the practices and whatnot. So he’s been engaged, and he’s been working out.” The Packers feel Jacobs is “in a pretty good spot,” LaFleur said. The Green Bay Packers ran for 57 yards against Dallas Green Bay ran 26 times for 57 yards Sunday, an average of 2.2 yards per carry. Pierre Strong Jr. had 11 carries for 28 yards. MarShawn Lloyd had eight for 10. On Sunday night, LaFleur called the run game “just too inconsistent.” On Monday, he said some of the blame went to the calls themselves. “Quite frankly, the concepts had no chance based on different front structures that they were presenting to us,” LaFleur said. “And they did a good job.” After the game, LaFleur said the Packers would keep running it. “We gotta keep hammering it because it is critical, I think in today’s football to be able to run the football,” LaFleur said. “It’s just hard on the pass game when you’re totally reliant on that.” Jacobs signed with Green Bay in 2024 after five seasons with the Raiders. He has not played since the end of the 2025 season. The Packers (4-2) play the Lions at 3:25 p.m. CT Sunday on FOX. item.title: ‘We’re gonna get to see how good a coach Ryan Day is’: Dave Portnoy reacts to Julian Sayin injury
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Ohio State Buckeyes got some brutal news on Tuesday when head coach Ryan Day announced that star quarterback Julian Sayin is out indefinitely with an arm injury. Even one of the Buckeyes’ loudest critics felt bad about it. Barstool Sports founder and Michigan alum Dave Portnoy sent his well wishes to Sayin after the news broke. But in the middle of an ongoing feud with Day, he also couldn’t resist taking another shot at the Ohio State head coach. Sayin Out Indefinitely Sayin was injured in the fourth quarter of Ohio State’s 19-15 win over the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday after he was sacked. He returned to the sideline with his right arm in a sling. On Tuesday, Day said that Sayin is out “indefinitely” and is “doubtful” to return during the regular season. The Buckeyes are now preparing for the possibility that last season’s Heisman Trophy finalist won’t play again this season. True freshman Luke Fahey is expected to take over under center after replacing Sayin during Saturday’s game, but sophomore Tavien St. Clair will get reps during practice, as well. After a bye this week, the Buckeyes close the regular season against USC, Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, and, of course, Michigan. Portnoy vs. Ryan Day Portnoy has never been shy about criticizing Day, but things have gotten more personal since he was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff pregame show earlier this month. He blamed Day and the Buckeyes for the decision, claiming that Ohio State “[complained] and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice” in a post on X . He also referred to Day as “Cryin Ryan.” Ahead of Saturday’s game, Portnoy took things a step further , arguing that Indiana’s Curt Cignetti is a far better coach than Day. “Cignetti is clearly a superstar coach, and it doesn’t matter where he went. Ryan Day would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State,” Portnoy said during Barstool’s weekend preview . Echoing former Michigan head coach Jim Harbaugh’s famous jab, Portnoy added, “Ryan Day was born on third base.” When Buckeyes fans pushed back, Portnoy called them “delusional and insane and sensitive” and claimed that Ohio State has “a Dave Portnoy fetish.” Then Day went out and beat Cignetti anyway. ‘This sucks’ Despite his obvious feud with Day and his disdain for Ohio State, Portnoy had a classy reaction to the Sayin news on X shortly after Day’s announcement on Tuesday. “This sucks. You never want injuries to derail a season even for your arch enemy. Hope Sayin comes back better than ever. I guess we’re gonna get to see how good a coach Ryan Day is the rest of the way,” Portnoy wrote . Obviously, Portnoy couldn’t help but throw in the subtle jab at Day, but it was a mostly classy message nonetheless. The post ‘We’re gonna get to see how good a coach Ryan Day is’: Dave Portnoy reacts to Julian Sayin injury appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Lip readers figured out what 76ers' LeBron James said to Knicks heckler
item.description: Lip readers figured out what 76ers' LeBron James said to Knicks heckler originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New York Knicks fans aren't always known for their decorum when dealing with opposing players. These people have gone on to say a lot of insane things to stars who crossed paths with Jalen Brunson and Co. Their NBA Opening Night and Banner celebration was no different. One heckler had something to say to LeBron James, but the Philadelphia 76ers star lashed back. It was hard to make out what The King said, but lip readers figured it out in a second. What 76ers' James said to the bothersome Knicks heckler on NBA Opening Night LeBron James commands respect from all types of NBA fans. In fact, he is the most well-known and loved ambassador of the game among all active players. Knicks fans do not care. Beyond the Knicks crowd shouting, "We don't want you!" at James when he was shooting free throws, one fan took it a step further. He got the 76ers veteran's attention from the stands and started trading words. James wasn't having any of the shenanigans the Knicks heckler unleashed. He apparently even corrected what the fan was saying. Apparently, they were claiming that James was from the West Coast instead of Ohio, via Legion Hoops. LeBron to a fan: “I’m not from the west coast, I’m from Ohio baby, f*ck is you talking about?” https://t.co/EhLEKUyZ5b — Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) October 21, 2026 The 76ers veteran was visibly livid with how bad the Knicks heckler was at being his team's sixth man. With the Knicks crowd on him all night, the frustration only grew. However, none of this seemed to affect James or the 76ers. James played 34 minutes and braved the Knicks crowd. He scored 14 points on 38.5% from the field despite going 0% from three-point range on three attempts. He also shot 67% from the free-throw line. James didn't just thrive on scoring. He dropped seven assists to get guys like Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and V.J. Edgecombe going. Defensively, the 76ers saw James do great despite being in Year 24. He grabbed four rebounds while getting a steal and a block. The Knicks crowd can be rough and affect a player's production, as evidenced by James efficiency woes on NBA Opening Night. item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
